title: White Rice with Tomatoes and/or Tomato-Based Sauce, Fat Added

content.title: About
content.content: This is boiled white rice prepared with tomatoes or a tomato‑based sauce and a modest amount of fat (oil or butter). The tomato component gives the dish a bright flavor and aroma, while the fat makes it more satisfying and helps absorb fat‑soluble vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
The rice‑tomato sauce combination is traditional in Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, and Latin American cuisines.
Adding a small amount of fat enhances flavor and improves the absorption of lycopene from tomatoes.
White rice is a staple energy source in many cultures and often serves as a neutral base for more flavorful ingredients.
Tomato sauce can be made from fresh or canned tomatoes; both retain most of the nutrients.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice provides quick‑digesting carbohydrates that are readily converted to glucose, supporting energy levels.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C and lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes in the sauce supply vitamin C and lycopene, which support immunity and protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Improved nutrient absorption
items.content: Fat aids the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) and carotenoids from the tomatoes.

items.title: Low sodium when homemade
items.content: Preparing the dish without excessive salt keeps sodium moderate, beneficial for blood pressure control.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: While rice contains modest protein, the combination with tomato sauce makes the meal more balanced.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or tomato juice.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Excessive added fat increases the calorie density of the dish and may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Additives in commercial sauce
items.content: When using ready‑made tomato sauces, check the label for added sugars, preservatives, or excess sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve as a side dish with meat, fish, or vegetable mains. Garnish with fresh herbs (basil, parsley) or spices (paprika, black pepper) to boost flavor. For extra protein, mix with beans or lentils.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. It can be frozen for up to 2 months after cooling and placed in a freezer‑safe bag.
